catalogue.name: p-adic Hodge theory and Fontaine’s period rings
catalogue.datesNote: Fontaine’s 1979 filtered-module work is a precursor; the 1982 Annals paper and Fontaine–Laffaille paper establish the dated period-ring and representation milestones. The 1988 Bures seminar was published as Astérisque 223 in 1994.
catalogue.why: Fontaine’s period rings and filtered modules relate p-adic Galois representations to de Rham and crystalline invariants, creating a bridge between arithmetic and cohomology.
works: J.-M. Fontaine, Sur certains types de représentations p-adiques du groupe de Galois d’un corps local, Ann. Math. 115 (1982), https://annals.math.princeton.edu/1982/115-3/p03
J.-M. Fontaine and G. Laffaille, Construction de représentations p-adiques, Ann. Sci. ENS 15 (1982), https://www.numdam.org/item/ASENS_1982_4_15_4_547_0/
J.-M. Fontaine, Périodes p-adiques (Séminaire de Bures, 1988), Astérisque 223 (1994), https://smf.emath.fr/publications/periodes-p-adiques-seminaire-de-bures-1988-reedition-2020
catalogue.basis: Primary journal records (Annals of Mathematics; Numdam) and the Société Mathématique de France publication record. The 1982 date applies to Fontaine’s period-ring framework, not to every later p-adic comparison theorem.

record.canonicalName: p-adic Hodge theory and Fontaine’s period rings

milestones.label: Filtered modules and Barsotti–Tate rings
milestones.work: J.-M. Fontaine, Modules galoisiens, modules filtrés et anneaux de Barsotti-Tate, Astérisque 65 (1979)
milestones.description: An earlier filtered-module framework for p-adic Galois representations.

evidence.claim: Astérisque 65 published Fontaine’s filtered-module work in 1979

milestones.note: Precursor to the period-ring milestone; it does not date the later comparison theory.

milestones.label: Fontaine publishes the period-ring framework
milestones.work: J.-M. Fontaine, Sur certains types de représentations p-adiques du groupe de Galois d’un corps local, Ann. Math. 115 (1982)
milestones.description: Constructs a Barsotti–Tate period ring and develops classes of p-adic local Galois representations.

evidence.claim: Annals published Fontaine’s period-ring paper in 1982

milestones.note: Dates this concrete framework, not the origin of every ingredient of p-adic Hodge theory.

milestones.label: Fontaine–Laffaille construct p-adic representations
milestones.work: J.-M. Fontaine and G. Laffaille, Construction de représentations p-adiques, Ann. Sci. ENS 15 (1982)
milestones.description: Uses filtered Dieudonné modules to explicitly construct p-adic Galois representations under stated hypotheses.

evidence.claim: The 1982 paper constructs representations from filtered modules; its abstract and introduction state the conditions and applications

milestones.note: An early explicit application, not a claim that all p-adic comparison theorems were proved in 1982.

milestones.label: Bures seminar published as Périodes p-adiques
milestones.work: J.-M. Fontaine, Périodes p-adiques (Séminaire de Bures, 1988), Astérisque 223 (1994)
milestones.description: The published seminar volume assembles period rings, representation classes, and comparisons among p-adic cohomology theories.

evidence.claim: The SMF describes the 1994 Astérisque volume and its 1988 seminar origin

milestones.note: 1994 is the volume’s publication year; the seminar met in 1988.

works.citation: Sur certains types de représentations p-adiques du groupe de Galois d’un corps local

record.notes: Focused primary-source addition. The event date marks the documented 1982 period-ring framework; Fontaine’s 1979 filtered-module paper remains a precursor. The 1988 seminar appeared in print in 1994.

catalogue.name: Euler formulates the equations of fluid motion
catalogue.datesNote: Euler wrote the memoir in 1755; it was published in 1757. The map uses the public publication year.
catalogue.why: Euler expressed fluid motion through general analytic equations and examined velocity fields and boundary conditions, helping establish mathematical fluid mechanics.
works: L. Euler, Principes généraux du mouvement des fluides, Mémoires de l’académie des sciences de Berlin 11 (1757), 274–315, https://scholarlycommons.pacific.edu/euler-works/226/
catalogue.basis: University of the Pacific Euler Archive work record and digitized original. It distinguishes the 1755 writing date from the 1757 publication date.

record.canonicalName: Euler formulates the equations of fluid motion

milestones.label: General equations for moving fluids published
milestones.work: L. Euler, Principes généraux du mouvement des fluides, Mémoires de l’académie des sciences de Berlin 11 (1757)
milestones.description: Euler presents general analytic equations for fluid motion in the memoir published in 1757.

evidence.claim: The Euler Archive dates the original memoir to 1757 and identifies its analytic treatment of fluid motion
evidence.source: University of the Pacific Euler Archive

milestones.note: The archive gives 1755 as the written date; 1757 is the public publication date.

milestones.label: Vortex flows and boundary conditions examined
milestones.work: L. Euler, Principes généraux du mouvement des fluides, Mémoires de l’académie des sciences de Berlin 11 (1757)
milestones.description: The same memoir studies vortex-flow examples and the role of boundary conditions.

evidence.claim: The Euler Archive summarizes the memoir’s vortex examples and early boundary-condition remarks
evidence.source: University of the Pacific Euler Archive

milestones.note: Application within the same published work, not a separate later discovery.

works.citation: Principes généraux du mouvement des fluides
works.whyItMatters: Published the general analytic treatment of fluid motion

record.notes: MSC2020 category 76 identifies fluid mechanics as a distinct mathematical subject. The Euler Archive records 1755 as the writing date and 1757 as the publication date.

catalogue.name: Chebyshev’s theory of best uniform approximation
catalogue.datesNote: An original St Petersburg imprint is dated 1857 in the ETH Library copy; a later journal-volume citation often gives 1859.
catalogue.why: Chebyshev studied how closely functions can be represented by simpler ones while controlling the largest error, establishing a central problem of approximation theory.
works: P. Chebyshev, Sur les questions de minima qui se rattachent à la représentation approximative des fonctions, St Petersburg Academy imprint (1857), https://www.e-rara.ch/zut/content/titleinfo/29427162
catalogue.basis: ETH Library digitization of the original 1857 academy imprint; MSC2020 class 41 identifies approximation and expansion theory as a distinct subject.

record.canonicalName: Chebyshev’s theory of best uniform approximation

milestones.label: Best approximation memoir printed
milestones.work: P. Chebyshev, Sur les questions de minima qui se rattachent à la représentation approximative des fonctions, St Petersburg Academy imprint (1857)
milestones.description: The memoir formulates minimum-deviation problems for approximate representation of functions.

evidence.claim: ETH Library holds an original academy imprint dated 1857 whose title identifies the minimum-deviation problem

milestones.note: This is an 1857 separate imprint; citations to the academy journal volume often give 1859.

works.citation: Sur les questions de minima qui se rattachent à la représentation approximative des fonctions

record.notes: Focused MSC2020 class 41 addition. The 1857 ETH Library imprint is used for the first public date; 1859 is a later volume citation.

catalogue.name: Babbage develops a calculus of functional equations

works: C. Babbage, An essay towards the calculus of functions, Philosophical Transactions (1815), https://makingscience.royalsociety.org/items/pt_9_23/paper-an-essay-towards-the-calculus-of-functions-by-c-charles-babbage
catalogue.basis: Dated original in a research library or academy archive; linked MSC2020 subject gap.
